title: On caring for user data: NeoVim caused Vim undo files to be deleted
why_read: A real data-loss incident report about Neovim deleting Vim undo files, useful for anyone who cares about backward-compatibility footguns in widely used editors.
analysis: This describes an incident where Neovim's handling of undo files caused unintended deletion of Vim's undo history, raising questions about compatibility assumptions between forks of a shared codebase. It matters because undo files can represent hours of unsaved editing history, and silent data loss bugs in ubiquitous tools like Vim/Neovim affect huge numbers of developers. The high comment count suggests substantial community debate over blame, responsibility, and how forks should treat shared file formats. This is a good case study in software stewardship and defensive design around user data.
